title: Review to Ensure Continued Relevance of GCE “A" Level Curriculum for Singapore Schools
what_it_is: Review to Ensure Continued Relevance of GCE “A" Level Curriculum for Singapore Schools

sections.label: A Level and IBDP pathways
sections.summary: MOE states the A Level, IBDP and Polytechnic diploma programmes are different pathways, and it reviews the A Level curriculum and overall curriculum and assessment demand.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The GCE “A” Level programme, International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) and Polytechnic diploma programmes are different pathways that offer choice and opportunities for students of different interests and profiles.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: MOE regularly reviews the GCE “A” Level curriculum to ensure its continued relevance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In addition, we are also in the midst of reviewing the overall curriculum and assessment demand across the general education system to identify ways to further strengthen the development of 21st Century Competencies in our students.

sections.label: A Level students entering polytechnics
sections.summary: A Level students admitted to Polytechnics may get advanced standings, some entering the second year, and universities are looking at micro-credentialing, with SIT conceptualising it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Some of them do decide to subsequently go into the Polytechnics and when the Polytechnics admit these students, they get some advanced standings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Some of the students who are admitted with their GCE “A” Level qualifications go straight to the second year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: It really depends on the credentials that the GCE “A” Level students come in with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We are also looking at how we can develop this whole concept of micro-credentialing with our Universities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: For example, SIT has started with conceptualising micro-credentialing, in which students will take modules at different points in time, during their career.

sections.label: June papers and languages
sections.summary: June papers tend to focus more on languages, and looking into that possibility depends on the number of students it is made available to.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: So, the June papers tend to focus more on the languages.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We can look into that possibility, but, really, it is also dependent on the number of students that we want to make it available to.
